spec_match.rationale: The fictional navigator.mcpServer probe is gone. Tools are registered on document.modelContext and invoked with executeTool(); the MCP tools/call framing is shown as what an agent would send, separate from the real call.

interactive.rationale: Tool buttons (aria-pressed), generated fields, Invoke and Clear all work; outputs are deterministic, not random.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Lede and index describe the three hops (agent tools/call, executeTool, MCP result) that the trace shows.

edge_cases.rationale: Missing required input is caught before executeTool and returned as isError; a throwing tool (bad expression, unknown directory) rejects with OperationError and maps to isError; XSS input renders literally.

references.rationale: Adds the WebMCP spec link beside ChromeStatus and MCP.

conformance.rationale: Unchanged suite (immutable). Flag on, all 6 assertions run against a real document.modelContext; flag off, every guarded assertion passes vacuously and registertool-rejects-tool-without-name passes only because document.modelContext is undefined. Needs a human decision; the page no longer contradicts the suite (it targets document.modelContext).

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chrome for Testing 158.0.8127.36 driven by Node Playwright against the local server, with and without --enable-experimental-web-platform-features, at 360x740 DPR3 touch and 1280x800. chrome-devtools-mcp is not available in this cloud environment, so this is NOT DevTools-MCP verification (rule 7b) and no accessibility-tree dump was taken; DOM semantics (roles, aria-pressed, label.control, live regions) were checked by script. Flag on, the deliberate throwing-tool paths make Chrome log "WebMCP tool execution failed" (documented on the page); otherwise 0 console errors, 0 failed requests, 0px overflow (a 31px mobile overflow from the tool list was found and fixed in this pass).

telemetry_health.rationale: The page now reports window.showcaseTelemetry.support("document.modelContext", supported|flag|unsupported) from its capability check, on top of the shared runtime error capture. No interaction events.

design_system.rationale: Variables and paired button colours; readable in screenshot.

accessibility.rationale: Tools are native buttons with aria-pressed, labels associated via for/id with aria-required on required fields, trace is role=log aria-live=polite.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px overflow at 360x740 DPR3 and 1280x800; every control >= 44px tall under pointer: coarse; param grid stacks under 480px.

openQuestions.title: Flag for a human: WebMCP conformance suite passes vacuously without the flag
openQuestions.detail: Conformance is immutable, so this needs a human. Without document.modelContext every guarded assertion passes and registertool-rejects-tool-without-name passes only on a TypeError from reading undefined. A suite that marks the flag-off state blocked, and asserts getTools()/executeTool(), duplicate-name InvalidStateError and AbortSignal unregistration (all verified on Chrome 158 + flag), would be honest.

openQuestions.title: Re-verify with chrome-devtools-mcp (Canary + WebMCP flag) and inspect the accessibility tree
openQuestions.detail: The 2026-11-24 fix pass used Playwright headless Chrome for Testing 158 because chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in the cloud environment.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible live log region announcing appended status rows; toggle button aria-pressed
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use aria-pressed for toggle state, associate every <label> with its control via for/id, and announce dynamic results through one polite live region or <output>.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: role=status on the mode banner, role=log + aria-live=polite on traces, <output> for results and meters, aria-pressed on selectable buttons, for/id labels on generated fields.

guidanceConsulted.query: toggle button group with minimum touch target size; controls without horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Size targets with min-block-size/min-inline-size from a --target-size token (24px, 44px under pointer: coarse) and let grid tracks shrink (minmax(0, 1fr)) so nothing overflows at 320-360px.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: --target-size token with @media (pointer: coarse) at 44px; minmax(0, …) tracks and min-inline-size: 0 on grid children. Measured 0px overflow and no control under 44px at 360x740.

summary: Fixed 2026-11-24: the page now uses the real WebMCP surface (document.modelContext registerTool/getTools/executeTool) when Chrome exposes it, and a labelled spec-shaped stand-in (v146/webmcp/webmcp-live.js) otherwise, with the flag and origin-trial steps on the page. Remaining gaps: the immutable conformance suite passes vacuously without the flag (human decision) and the run was not DevTools-MCP verified.
